items.title: Know Your Lines - trauma radiograph quick reference
items.summary: Two printable crib sheets of the lines, angles and ratios you are supposed to measure on a trauma film and probably eyeball instead.

_homepage.note: The adult sheet runs wrist, elbow, knee, hip, ankle and C-spine; the paediatric one covers elbow ossification centres, Baumann angle, fat pad signs and Salter-Harris, which is exactly where a registrar's uncertainty lives at 3am. Feldman-Kiss, Griffiths and Long built them as bedside prompts rather than imaging rules, with the explicit caveat that projection and skeletal maturity move the numbers. This is the sort of thing worth printing once and pinning above the PACS terminal.

items.title: SGEM#523: Clinical guidelines for faltering weight
items.summary: The structured skeptical treatment of a brand-new AAP/NASPGHAN guideline, built around a seven-month-old sent to the ED for a failure-to-thrive workup.

_homepage.note: Faltering weight arrives in the ED as a referral rather than a diagnosis, and the question is almost always how much workup belongs to you tonight versus the paediatric clinic next week. Dennis Ren walks the 2026 guideline's recommendations on diagnostic and feeding strategies, including whether socioeconomic status should count as a diagnostic risk factor at all. The SGEM's format means you get the critical appraisal of the evidence base, not just the recommendation list.

items.title: Surprise Chef pick out their film score inspirations
items.summary: The Melbourne instrumental group name the Italian soundtrack records behind Frogs In A Pond, which lands today.

_homepage.note: Fifth album, first for Concord Jazz after the Big Crown run, and cut almost entirely live across nine consecutive days with minimal overdubs - the kind of session detail that explains why their records sit well on a turntable. The reference points they pick out are Piero Umiliani and Piero Piccioni, which places this beside the library's soundtrack shelf as much as its soul one. Local band, out today, and the Northside shops will have it.

items.title: Strike cancelled after doctors reach last-minute deal
items.summary: The twelve-hour Victorian stoppage planned for Wednesday is off, and the interim deal that bought it off is squarely about doctors in training.

_homepage.note: The headline terms land on registrars specifically: recording and payment of overtime that doctors in training have been working unpaid, a maximum rostered duty period cut to thirteen consecutive hours, and limits on consecutive days above twelve and a half. The pay component - six per cent and a $5,000 payment for DiTs - sits a long way below the twenty-eight per cent over four years that was being asked, and ASMOF's Kevin Shi has already said it falls far short. It runs twelve months, which parks the real fight on the far side of the November state election.

items.title: Jalen Ngonda's Doctrine of Love is a love letter to soul
items.summary: The Daptone singer on writing his second record in hotel rooms and on the tour bus, and on the misread certificate that gave it its title.

_homepage.note: Ngonda is already on the shelf, and this sits right next to the Sharon Jones, Menahan Street Band and Thee Sacred Souls end of the collection - same label ecosystem, same Vince Chiarito and Michael Buckley production team as the debut. The interesting admission is how scattered the writing was compared to Come Around and Love Me, which was cut in one place with time to spare. He places this one closer to 1968 than the early-seventies feel of the first, which is audible once you are listening for it.

items.title: ARISE FLUIDS: Fluids, pressors, neither, both?
items.summary: An ANZ-run septic shock trial appraised by the one blogger who will tell you when a trial does not actually answer the question.

_homepage.note: ARISE FLUIDS was run out of Australian and New Zealand emergency departments, so the case mix and the resuscitation habits being tested are his own, not an American ICU's. Morgenstern's read is that the unblinded design leaves real room for bias, which is the kind of caveat that decides whether a result changes your practice on Monday or just your reading list. Worth pairing with the peripheral vasopressor material that has been circulating all month.

items.title: Forge your fit with A New Medium's FW26 collection
items.summary: A small-label autumn drop led by a waxed canvas Sportsman jacket, with trousers, outerwear and caps rounding it out.

_homepage.note: Waxed canvas is the rustic-menswear workhorse that sits between the Woolrich and Pendleton end of the reference shelf and anything RRL has done with a hunting silhouette. The Sportsman cut is the piece to look at here - it is the shape that justifies the cloth, rather than waxed cotton applied to a generic trucker. Heddels is the one source that will tell you the weight and the finish rather than just the price.

items.title: Brassai: Secret Paris
items.summary: More than 150 vintage prints the photographer made himself, half an hour up the Yarra at Bulleen, and it closes on 15 November.

_homepage.note: This is Brassai's first solo show in Australia in over fifty years, assembled with the Estate Brassai and including the night work, the graffiti pictures, the Surrealist experiments and rare copies of Paris de Nuit. The prints are the point: vintage, made in his own darkroom, which is a different object entirely from a modern reproduction. Heide's third modernist photography survey in five years after Lee Miller and the Man Ray/Max Dupain pairing, and there are three weekends left on it.

items.title: Enshrouded - Changelog for Hotfix 1.0.0.3
items.summary: The third hotfix since the 1.0 launch, and the one that finally hands back missing Early Access rewards from the pause menu.

_homepage.note: Straight from Keen rather than a site rewriting their notes: crash fixes around water simulation, factories and random events, a rare save-migration crash resolved, and characters with invalid backpack slots now migrating. If a Flame Altar came through in the wrong place, migration corrects it but the water has to be re-added by hand. The endless black screen on loading a multiplayer world is fixed too, and the corrupted-character-save fix is still in progress.

items.title: Melbourne's new entertainment precinct opens next week
items.summary: Spiegel Haus opens in Chinatown on 29 October with a 380-seat spiegeltent and a 400-seat black box, which is a lot of new room for a city that keeps losing venues.

_homepage.note: A two-level precinct built around a Belgian spiegeltent is an odd and welcome thing to put in the middle of the CBD, and the black box is configured for theatre, comedy and live music rather than any one of them. Worth knowing about now because opening-week programming is the cheapest way to find out whether the rooms actually sound good. It also lands in the same stretch as the Arden Central and Snakepit announcements, so the venue drought may be turning.

items.title: Claude designs protein binders against scorpion venom
items.summary: An AI model generated 318,484 candidate proteins in 64 hours and 17 of the 211 actually tested bound scorpion neurotoxins - an envenomation problem, not a chatbot demo.

_homepage.note: Scorpion stings hit about 1.2 million people a year and antivenom is expensive and chronically short, which makes this a toxinology supply problem before it is an AI story. The two strongest candidates bound Cn2 at single-digit nanomolar affinity across two independent labs, and appear to sit near the epitope of a known neutralising antibody. Read the limits honestly though: these were recombinant toxins, nothing was tested for neutralisation in cells or animals, and no one has produced an antivenom here.

items.title: Giving small negatives the justice they deserve
items.summary: A defence of 110 that argues the format's bad reputation is mostly a processing and scanning failure, with the frames to back it.

_homepage.note: The argument generalises well beyond 110: most of what gets blamed on a small negative is actually lab handling and a scanner resolving less than the film holds. Useful discipline if you ever shoot half-frame or crop hard off 35mm, since the same corrections apply. Tinyframetales files it under gear theory, but it reads as a scanning tutorial with a chip on its shoulder.
